alcove-20260729-ad409ff3.title: Add a read-only radar explain command for missing or excluded items

alcove-20260729-ad409ff3.value: Gives owners and agents a fast, user-visible diagnostic path for radar trust: why did this item appear, why was it filtered out, or which source failed before it could be considered.
evidence: docs/radars.md:11-22 documents per-radar cache/raw.json, scored.json, run.json, reports, OKF index, and events as durable run artifacts.
docs/radars.md:66-68 says radar run fetches enabled sources, deduplicates by URL/title, scores with the profile, writes cache/reports, writes OKF index, and appends a run event.

src/alcove/radars/scoring.py:20-44 records stale, blocked keyword, score, score_reason, and included=false/true decisions.
src/alcove/cli.py:270-300 exposes radar list, init, run, status, and preset list, but no explain/diagnose command over the existing run artifacts.

alcove-20260729-ad409ff3.recommendedApproach: Recommended: add a read-only `RadarModule.explain(...)` module interface and `alcove radar explain <radar-id> --query <text|url> [--date YYYY-MM-DD] --json`. It should read existing raw.json, scored.json, and run.json, classify the likely pipeline stage, and return matched raw/scored rows with source_id, score, score_reason, included, report presence, failed source context, and cache paths compacted for display.
alternatives: Expose a broader `alcove radar inspect <radar-id>` command that prints the latest run artifact paths and counts only. Smaller, but less useful when diagnosing one missing item.
Add the diagnostic only to the dashboard radar page. More visual, but CLI-first is easier to verify and better for agents.
acceptanceCriteria: A read-only radar diagnostic module interface can explain latest-run and selected-date runs without fetching sources or invoking AI.

`alcove radar explain <radar-id> --query <needle> --json` reports whether matching items were not in raw cache, fetched but excluded, included but report-limited/deduped, or blocked by source/run failure evidence.

nonGoals: No live web fetches in tests.
No scoring, ranking, preset, notification, or AI summary behavior changes.
No sports/news/stock domain-specific ranking changes.
No mutation of radar definitions or cache artifacts.

alcove-20260730-4493364a.title: Make service tick resilient with per-module step isolation
alcove-20260730-4493364a.problem: The scheduled service tick is the local maintenance backbone, but its implementation calls connectors, watchers, blogs, radars, automations, publishers, mounts, OKF build, health, usage, pruning, and dashboard build in one linear method. Several tests prove individual malformed inputs are tolerated, but a raised exception from an unchecked step can still prevent later maintenance, task-health reporting, usage recording, and dashboard refresh.
alcove-20260730-4493364a.whyNow: The docs describe `alcove service tick` as the deterministic scheduler path, and README/docs list it as the maintenance command. The code already has a task-health summary interface, so preserving partial progress and reporting the failed step would directly improve an existing user-visible operational surface.
alcove-20260730-4493364a.value: A single bad blog, radar, publisher, mount, or connector run would degrade one module instead of making the whole scheduled tick brittle. Users get fresher dashboard and health data, and maintainers get better locality for diagnosing which module failed.

src/alcove/service.py:151-190 performs every maintenance module sequentially before usage recording and dashboard build.
src/alcove/service.py:240-330 already converts module payloads into task-health status, which could represent caught per-step failures.
tests/test_service.py:111-237 covers malformed radar, connector, publisher, mount, and project data tolerance, showing reliability is already an expected service-tick contract.
docs/usage.md:487-497 documents `alcove service tick --home ~/.alcove --json` and skip flags as the scheduler/manual maintenance path.
alcove-20260730-4493364a.recommendedApproach: Introduce a small internal service tick step runner module behind the ServiceModule.tick interface. Each step should return a normalized payload with status, metrics, and error text; unexpected exceptions should be caught per step, marked failed, and allow remaining independent steps plus dashboard/usage/task-health finalization to continue. Keep existing JSON keys stable.
alternatives: Only wrap the highest-risk external IO steps first: connectors, watchers, blogs, radars, automations, publishers, and mounts.
Add fail-fast mode as an opt-in debug flag, but keep scheduler default resilient.
acceptanceCriteria: A forced exception in one independent tick step is represented under that module's payload and task_health.checks without aborting later independent steps.
Dashboard snapshot, usage rollups, and task_health are still written when one independent module fails.
Existing service tick JSON keys remain compatible for successful runs.
Tests cover at least one failing step and one later step still running.
Verification runs focused service tests plus scripts/smoke.sh and scripts/check.sh.
risks: Catching too broadly could hide programming errors unless failure payloads and logs are explicit.
Some steps may have real ordering dependencies; the slice should preserve current ordering and only isolate independent failures.
nonGoals: Do not redesign launchd installation.
Do not change scheduler cadence or add background model calls.
Do not rewrite all maintenance modules.
